title: What is a game ?
author: Ok-Investment4414
selftext:
Like for real,this isn't a philosophical debate we don't like slop. Realistically what can be called a game and is it up to the dev or the player (buyer) .  
   
Paddle Paddle Paddle grossed over 1M Usd in revenue and it's slop.

comments.author: Beskull
comments.body:
I call a game, loops and gravity. 
Loop cycles that are entertaining and fun. 
Gravity that keeps the players in the game and coming back when they aren't playing. 

Simple objective(s) and interactions to achieve that

comments.author: West_Satisfaction299
comments.body: To me I think, as long as there are people who want to play a game you made. Then it counts as a game. Out here in Asia, the number of AI YouTube videos being created is crazy but also the number of people who watch them. I'm referring specifically to old Chinese comic books turned into TV Shows.

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body: This video covers, (for me) how simple a game can be. A game can be a lot of things, but it needs to be fun and something people want to play. [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QlMMST6Pte4](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QlMMST6Pte4)

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
Slop, imo, is a measure of quality and polish. It's deservedly derogatory when someone is trying to publish a game that is still in the slop stage. However the community needs to lay off people for showcasing slop that they're still working on. If you have slop, and you're taking time to refine it, and improve it, and turn it into something that's your own unique thing... then that's great. One day it won't be slop. Hell, minecraft was slop when it released in early alpha, and I think it's the most selling game ever (and it's not particularly close), but it made huge improvements over the first two years.

Posting  slop here looking for feedback on how to improve should be met with assistance. Critique is probably well earned, but should be delivered kindly, not like someone stepped on their baby.  

If, on the other hand, someone is posting their game's Steam/Itch link that they one-shotted, and is clearly an unpolished mess (likely a worse-in-all-ways copy of some other successful game) then I don't think you need to go out of your way to be nice about it. That quick slop flop attitude is going to burnout the entire game industry on AI anything and makes the job harder for everyone who wants to succeed in the industry (and these people aren't making money doing it --- well maybe in the phone market, I don't know what the tolerance of those buyers is like, but Honor of Kings making \~20 billion dollars makes me wonder.

comments.author: RossRiskDabbler
comments.body:
A game solves a commercial problem where folks have been looking to "do that", where-ever it is released at that time. 

No different than RTS in the 90s with command and conquer where people wanted to "conquer the world" and "the 00s with tony hawk" where people wanted to do impossible stunts. It solves a problem. A need that people want/seek.
